page.title: Work
page.intro: My enterprise work belongs to the companies I did it for. These products I build on my own time, and every decision, tradeoff and test in them is open to you: the customer, the decisions, where the evidence overruled my plan, the architecture and how I validate it.
caseStudy.col.question: Question
bookshelfai.tagline: Photograph a shelf, get a library.
bookshelfai.summary: For people who genuinely love books: capture several books from one photo while browsing or traveling, then keep one library across wishlist, owned and read. Every AI scan has a real cost, so accuracy, convenience and price are decided together. I own it end to end, building with AI development agents while making every product and technical call myself.
bookshelfai.role: Sole product owner, designer and builder
bookshelfai.problem.heading: Book lovers don’t want to type in their books.
bookshelfai.problem.intro: A deliberately niche audience: people who buy, borrow and browse books constantly. Most cataloguing apps assume one book at a time and a barcode. The real jobs were messier, and they set the product thesis.
bookshelfai.problem.item_1.title: Capture books while browsing
bookshelfai.problem.item_1.body: In a shop, a library or a friend’s house: fast, one-handed, sometimes offline.
bookshelfai.problem.item_2.title: Scan several books at once
bookshelfai.problem.item_2.body: Spines, not barcodes. Many books per photo, reviewed in bulk.
bookshelfai.problem.item_3.title: One library, start to finish
bookshelfai.problem.item_3.body: Wishlist, owned and read in one place, instead of a note, a spreadsheet and a reading app.
bookshelfai.decisions.heading: Scan → identify → confirm → lifecycle.
bookshelfai.decisions.item_1.title: One scan flow, not modes
bookshelfai.decisions.item_1.body: No “cover mode” versus “shelf mode.” The model infers how many books are in frame, and a single-book photo stays the simplest case.
bookshelfai.decisions.item_2.title: Confirm before commit
bookshelfai.decisions.item_2.body: Bulk review with work-level de-duplication and partial-failure handling, so one unreadable spine never sinks a whole shelf.
bookshelfai.decisions.item_3.title: Wishlist to read, in one place
bookshelfai.decisions.item_3.body: A book found while browsing becomes a wishlist item, then a book on the shelf, then a book read: one lifecycle instead of three apps.
bookshelfai.tradeoffs.heading: Every scan has a real cost.
bookshelfai.tradeoffs.row_1.question: Does this need a price plan?
bookshelfai.tradeoffs.row_1.decision: Yes. Pricing is designed alongside the inference cost, with explicit credits for enhanced scans
bookshelfai.tradeoffs.row_1.why: A product with per-use AI cost is only viable if what customers pay covers what each scan costs.
bookshelfai.tradeoffs.row_2.question: Which model per scan?
bookshelfai.tradeoffs.row_2.decision: A lower-cost model by default, with a stronger-model retry on request
bookshelfai.tradeoffs.row_2.why: Most scans don’t need the expensive model. Hard ones still get it.
bookshelfai.tradeoffs.row_3.question: When does a retry cost credit?
bookshelfai.tradeoffs.row_3.decision: Only when the retry actually identifies a book
bookshelfai.tradeoffs.row_3.why: Customers shouldn’t pay for the model’s misses.
bookshelfai.tradeoffs.row_4.question: Trust the model’s titles?
bookshelfai.tradeoffs.row_4.decision: Validate against external book data and de-duplicate at the work level
bookshelfai.tradeoffs.row_4.why: Structured sources beat a plausible hallucination, and accuracy is part of what customers pay for.
bookshelfai.tradeoffs.row_5.question: Which markets first?
bookshelfai.tradeoffs.row_5.decision: The US and Canada, on a foundation built for global use
bookshelfai.tradeoffs.row_5.why: Privacy, localization and globalization are designed in, so other countries need compliance tuning rather than a rebuild, and starting narrower reaches the market faster.
bookshelfai.evidence.heading: The request worked. The experience didn’t.
bookshelfai.evidence.item_1.title: Success nobody noticed
bookshelfai.evidence.item_1.body: In testing, people missed that a scan had succeeded. The request returned fine, but the moment didn’t register. I traced the full interaction, separated functional success from experience success, and redesigned the feedback instead of calling it done.
bookshelfai.evidence.item_2.title: Engagement features, deferred
bookshelfai.evidence.item_2.body: Recommendations and notifications wait until core retention is validated. Adding engagement features before the core habit exists would hide whether the product actually works.
bookshelfai.system.heading: The server is the authority.
bookshelfai.system.intro: AI calls, identity, data and spending controls all live on the server, so credentials stay protected and model cost stays a product decision rather than a client-side accident. Offline capture is deliberately bounded: enough to be useful on the go, never enough to move sensitive work onto the device. That is the opposite choice from BC Arcade, because the products need different things.
bookshelfai.system.node_1.title: Clients
bookshelfai.system.node_2.title: Edge
bookshelfai.system.node_3.title: API service
bookshelfai.system.node_3.detail: Auth, orchestration, rate limits, spending controls
bookshelfai.system.node_4.title: Services
bookshelfai.system.node_4.detail: Vision model to identify · book-data APIs to enrich · PostgreSQL
bookshelfai.system.bullet_1: Clients never call the model directly, which protects credentials and caps unauthorized model use
bookshelfai.system.bullet_2: Google sign-in with rotating access and refresh tokens and server-side revocation
bookshelfai.system.bullet_3: Bounded offline capture: scans queue safely without connectivity and resolve on the server
bookshelfai.system.bullet_4: Separate development and production sign-in, databases and release-tagged error monitoring
bookshelfai.validation.heading: Quality without a large team.
bookshelfai.validation.para_1: Automated pull-request checks, security tests, monitoring, logs, performance diagnostics and release controls stand between a change and a release. AI coding agents speed up the implementation, but the direction, architecture, review, debugging and validation are mine.
bookshelfai.validation.para_2: When a production health check kept failing in CI, I traced it to the edge network rather than the app, separated application availability from infrastructure filtering, and questioned whether that check belonged in pull-request CI at all, instead of just silencing it.
bookshelfai.built.heading: All of it, with AI agents as the multiplier, not the decision-maker.
bc-arcade.tagline: Play for a few minutes, then put it down.
bc-arcade.summary: Short, satisfying games for people who want to enjoy a quick session and move on with their day. The lineup is familiar games, independently built and reworked where playtesting called for it. I own the strategy, UX, architecture, implementation, testing, release and production quality, using AI coding agents while reviewing every behavior, test and change myself.
bc-arcade.role: Sole product owner, designer and builder
bc-arcade.problem.heading: A good session should end on the player’s terms.
bc-arcade.problem.intro: The audience is casual players who want a brief, satisfying game and then want to put the phone down. Everything else follows from that.
bc-arcade.problem.item_1.title: Brief, satisfying sessions
bc-arcade.problem.item_1.body: Games that reward a few minutes of play, without tricks to stretch them into an hour.
bc-arcade.problem.item_2.title: No freemium pressure
bc-arcade.problem.item_2.body: No energy meters, timers or paywalls in the middle of play. Premium is a clear purchase, not a nag.
bc-arcade.problem.item_3.title: No wagering
bc-arcade.problem.item_3.body: Stakes come from scores and objectives, never real money.
bc-arcade.decisions.heading: Familiar games, reworked where it matters.
bc-arcade.decisions.item_1.title: Familiar, not invented
bc-arcade.decisions.item_1.body: These are independently built versions of games people already know. The work is in the implementation, and in substantial changes where play called for them, as with Blackjack and Star Swarm.
bc-arcade.decisions.item_2.title: A reason to come back, not a reason to stay
bc-arcade.decisions.item_2.body: The Daily Challenge sets a fresh handful of goals across several games each day, with streaks. It invites a short return visit instead of a longer session.
bc-arcade.decisions.item_3.title: Tune systems, not vibes
bc-arcade.decisions.item_3.body: Hazards, enemies, difficulty and randomness are tuned against challenge, fairness, player control and replay value, with bounded, seeded randomness and explicit specs.
bc-arcade.evidence.heading: My plan, playtested and corrected.
bc-arcade.evidence.item_1.title: Blackjack had no tension
bc-arcade.evidence.item_1.body: Unlimited free chips meant nothing was at stake. Playtesting turned it into goal-based arcade play, which kept the tension without any money.
bc-arcade.evidence.item_2.title: My favorites weren’t the lineup
bc-arcade.evidence.item_2.body: I started with games I liked. Market research showed gaps, so Sort Puzzle and Daily Word were added, and Daily Word became part of the Daily Challenge.
bc-arcade.evidence.item_3.title: A standard I set made accessibility worse
bc-arcade.evidence.item_3.body: When a shared technical pattern I had prescribed made screen-reader behavior worse, the standard changed instead of every game being forced to follow it.
bc-arcade.system.heading: Offline-first, with the server guarding purchases.
bc-arcade.system.intro: Gameplay runs on the device, so it is instant and works without a connection. The server has authority only where it matters: paid entitlements and purchase ownership. BookshelfAI makes the opposite choice. The two apps share quality practices and some services, but each architecture is chosen for its product.
bc-arcade.system.bullet_1: Server-authoritative premium entitlements with signed tokens, offline grace, replay protection, restore and revocation
bc-arcade.system.bullet_2: An AI dependency-triage agent that merges only low-risk updates, after a deterministic guard layer re-verifies authorship, file paths, CI status, branch protection and the exact commit
bc-arcade.system.bullet_3: Seeded simulations, oracle comparisons and regret metrics to evaluate non-deterministic gameplay
bc-arcade.system.bullet_4: Frame-time and render measurement, Sentry breadcrumbs and in-app feedback to separate tuning from defects
bc-arcade.tradeoffs.heading: Every choice has a failure mode.
bc-arcade.tradeoffs.row_1.question: Where does game state live?
bc-arcade.tradeoffs.row_1.decision: On the device, with only purchases checked by the server
bc-arcade.tradeoffs.row_1.why: Casual play has to be instant and work offline. Paid access is the part that needs a single source of truth.
bc-arcade.tradeoffs.row_2.question: How much should the AI agent merge?
bc-arcade.tradeoffs.row_2.decision: Only low-risk updates. Uncertainty escalates to the higher-risk tier
bc-arcade.tradeoffs.row_2.why: Safety beats maximum automation. The AI classifies, and deterministic checks decide.
bc-arcade.tradeoffs.row_3.question: How to make the app faster?
bc-arcade.tradeoffs.row_3.decision: Measure real release artifacts before removing anything
bc-arcade.tradeoffs.row_3.why: Baselines first. Rejected approaches are documented when the gain isn’t worth the loss.
bc-arcade.tradeoffs.row_4.question: Which markets first?
bc-arcade.tradeoffs.row_4.decision: The US and Canada, on a foundation built for global use
bc-arcade.tradeoffs.row_4.why: Privacy, localization and globalization are designed in, so other countries need compliance tuning rather than a rebuild.
bc-arcade.validation.heading: Release readiness is a product decision.
bc-arcade.validation.para_1: Randomness makes “does it work?” a statistical question. Repeatable seeded simulations, reference comparisons, blunder metrics and persona-level analysis across large samples show whether a game behaves as designed.
bc-arcade.validation.para_2: For a solo developer, automated gates are the team. Unit and end-to-end tests, seeded simulations, and security and release checks run on every pull request, while performance instrumentation and Sentry monitoring cover what ships. Failing gates get fixed, never bypassed.
bc-arcade.built.heading: Designed and built from the ground up.
